faq.q: Is November a good time to rent a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, if you want calm seas and fewer crowds. November air temperatures average 15–20°C, and sea temperatures stay around 17–19°C. You'll get plenty of sunny days, though you should check the wind forecast—Levante days can bring chop. Many boats still operate, and you'll often find better availability than in summer.

faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Marbella in November?
faq.a: The Mediterranean off Marbella in November typically ranges from 17°C to 19°C. That's still swimmable for the brave, but most guests prefer a wetsuit or just enjoy the sun on deck. If you're planning a swim, a midday charter will give you the warmest water.

faq.q: What should I wear for a November boat trip in Marbella?
faq.a: Layer up: a light jumper or fleece, a windproof jacket, and non-slip shoes. Even on sunny days, the breeze on the water can feel cool. Bring sunglasses and sunscreen—UV is still strong. If you plan to swim, a thin wetsuit or rash guard helps.

faq.q: Can I still swim on a November boat charter?
faq.a: Yes, but it's brisk. Sea temperatures around 18°C are common in November. Some guests do a quick dip, especially on sunny afternoons. If swimming is a priority, consider a shorter charter in the middle of the day when the sea is warmest, and bring a towel and change of clothes.

faq.q: How windy is Marbella in November?
faq.a: Average wind speeds are around 10–15 km/h, but Levante days can bring stronger gusts from the east, creating choppier seas. Westerly winds are generally calmer. Always check the marine forecast 24 hours before your charter. Our skippers will advise if conditions are unsafe—safety comes first.

faq.q: Does it rain a lot in Marbella in November?
faq.a: November is one of the wetter months, but still not rainy by northern European standards. Expect around 5–7 rainy days, usually short showers rather than all-day downpours. The rest of the month is often sunny. Booking a flexible charter with a free cancellation window (if available) is a smart move.

faq.q: Are all boats available in November?
faq.a: Most of our fleet is available year-round, including the Astondoa 40, Azimut 39, and Mangusta 80. Smaller boats like the Speedboat and Mariah SX21 also operate in November. However, some larger yachts may be in for maintenance. Contact us via WhatsApp for real-time availability.

faq.q: What is the best time of day for a November charter?
faq.a: Midday to early afternoon (12:00–16:00) is ideal—air and sea temps are at their highest, and the sun is strongest. You'll also get the best light for photos. Sunset charters are beautiful, but it gets cooler quickly after 17:00, so bring an extra layer.

data.body_html:
Thinking about a Marbella boat rental in November 2032? You're smart to check the weather first. November in Marbella is a shoulder month: cooler than summer but still mild, with plenty of sunny days. Sea temperatures hover around 17–19°C, air temps range from 15–20°C, and you'll avoid the summer crowds. This guide gives you the real numbers—wind, rain, daylight—plus practical tips for booking your November charter from Puerto Banús.

November Climate at a Glance

Marbella enjoys a microclimate sheltered by the Sierra Blanca and La Concha mountains. November averages:

  • Air temperature: 15–20°C (highs can reach 22°C on sunny days)
  • Sea temperature: 17–19°C
  • Rainfall: ~60 mm over 5–7 days, usually short showers
  • Wind: 10–15 km/h average; Levante can bring stronger gusts
  • Daylight: ~10 hours, sunrise ~07:45, sunset ~18:15

Compared to July's 30°C, November is noticeably cooler, but it's still far warmer than most of northern Europe. A sunny November day on the water is a delight—just bring layers.

Sea Temperature and Swimming

The Mediterranean off Marbella in November sits at about 18°C. That's a shock after summer's 24°C, but some guests still take a quick dip—especially on sheltered spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. If swimming is a must, book a midday charter when the sun has warmed the surface. A thin wetsuit or rash vest makes a big difference.

For a leisurely cruise without swimming, November is perfect. You'll have the coastline to yourself, and the light is beautiful for photography.

Wind and Sea Conditions

November's prevailing winds are light, but the Levante (east wind) can blow at 20–30 km/h, creating choppy seas. The Poniente (west wind) is usually calmer. Our skippers monitor forecasts closely and will recommend the safest route—often hugging the coast from Puerto Banús towards Estepona or Cabopino. If conditions look rough, we'll suggest rescheduling; your safety is non-negotiable.

What to Wear and Bring

  • Layers: fleece or light jumper, windproof jacket
  • Non-slip shoes (deck shoes or trainers)
  • Sunglasses and sunscreen (UV still strong)
  • Swimsuit and towel if you plan a dip
  • Camera or phone for the views

All our charters include water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks—so you don't need to bring drinks.

Best Boats for November

For a November charter, enclosed or partially covered boats offer more comfort. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) both have cockpits with wind protection—ideal for cooler days. If you want more space, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) has a saloon with heating. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a showstopper, and in November you might get it for a better rate.

For a budget-friendly option, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) is fun, but you'll feel the wind more—best for a sunny calm day.

Pricing and Value in November

November is off-peak, so you'll often find better availability and potentially lower rates than summer. Our Tier A boats—the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39—start at €749 for 2 hours and go up to €2,299 for 8 hours, including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and IVA. The Mangusta 80 (including the grey variant) is available from €4,719 for a 4-hour charter, with a jet ski included free.

For other boats like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86, pricing is on request—message us on WhatsApp for a tailored quote.

Booking Tips for November

  • Check the 7-day marine forecast before booking.
  • Book a midday slot (12:00–16:00) for the warmest hours.
  • Ask about flexible cancellation if weather looks uncertain.
  • Consider a longer charter—November days are shorter, so an 8-hour trip gives you time to explore.
  • Combine your boat trip with a walk around Puerto Banús or lunch at a chiringuito.

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella's marina. You can also plan a route to Cabopino or Estepona—both are beautiful in November.
